solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Referee's informant?

parts.note: a match official literally blows a whistle, and a person exposing wrongdoing at work is known by the same compound name

explanation.surface: Someone tipping off the match official about foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the informer's title literally: a referee is the person on the pitch who blows the whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: An employee who exposes wrongdoing to authorities is a classic informer, named after the referee's signal.

clue.text: Hit obstacle over work

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, that is above, the second

parts.note: a wall is an obstacle in one's path
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Striking a barrier placed above some building job.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a heavy blow is to thump or strike them hard, a colloquial sense.

clue.text: With the label showing, maybe, in great detail?

definitions.meaning: a garment worn reversed shows its label, being turned wrong side out
knowing something thoroughly, every part of it, is knowing it this way

explanation.surface: A shirt worn with its tag visible, described meticulously.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversed garment exposes its lining and tag; the idiom 'know it ___' means thorough knowledge.

clue.text: Mad hatters' warnings

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters of the following word go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Warnings issued by crazed hat-makers, nodding to the Mad Hatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing statements of intended harm serve as warnings of what may come.

clue.text: Horse riding in Times Square, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of the phrase are set out oddly in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone on horseback in the middle of New York's Times Square, an odd sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The skill or sport of riding on horseback, as in dressage or show jumping.

clue.text: Noble person sheltering someone who's poorly

indicators.note: the phrase Noble person shelters, or holds within it, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: An aristocrat taking in a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering from leprosy is ill, so loosely one who is unwell.

clue.text: Weather over England primarily produces misery

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so take the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: English weather making everyone miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or great sorrow is a synonym for misery.

clue.text: Degenerate holding back default

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read in the reverse direction
the word Degenerate holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A degenerate person keeping back a debt payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' marks the hidden run and 'back' says it is read from right to left within dEGENERate.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or fail to honour an agreement is to default on it.

clue.text: One failing to win quirky roles

indicators.note: quirky means odd or peculiar, so the letters are set out in a peculiar new order

explanation.surface: An actor who missed out on winning the unusual parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The defeated party in a contest is the one who did not win.

clue.text: Loads of hesitation with parking by young person

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a teen is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen

explanation.surface: A youngster hesitating a lot over parking.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for very many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Doctor reloads tests

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician reloads some medical tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Painful experiences that try one's endurance are trials or tests.

clue.text: Rearrange dance to follow religious studies

indicators.note: the dance is to follow, coming after, the abbreviation for religious studies

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject of religious studies
a jig is a lively folk dance

explanation.surface: A dance routine reorganised to come after a religion lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British verb meaning to reorganise or reset something differently.

clue.text: Black dog who gets around?

definitions.note: the definition is the person who gets around, a noun phrase

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour, as in jet-black
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A black dog that roams the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy traveller flying between fashionable resorts is someone who gets around the world.

clue.text: Sharp-eyed old maid, perhaps, smothers bachelor

indicators.note: smothers means covers up completely, so the old maid wraps round the bachelor's letter

parts.note: a maid is one example of a domestic servant
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: An old housemaid with keen eyes stifles an unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to notice things is watchful and sharp-eyed.

clue.text: Recasts troublesome performer

indicators.note: troublesome suggests disorder, so the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A director recasts a difficult actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who acts on stage or screen is a performer.

clue.text: Understanding one initially cunning strategy

parts.note: tact is sensitive understanding of how to treat people
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of the word cunning

explanation.surface: A sly plan built on one person's understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned move or method to achieve an aim is a manoeuvre or strategy.

clue.text: After operation, I swallowed a painkiller

indicators.note: after puts the following pieces behind the abbreviation for operation

parts.note: ate means consumed, swallowed

explanation.surface: A patient after surgery taking a pain-relief pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug derived from opium, like morphine, used to dull pain.

clue.text: Change feature of church for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out on air, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: the altar is the communion table, a central feature of a church

explanation.surface: Modifying part of a church service for radio or television.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify or make something different is to change it.

clue.text: A lot of fantasies not getting started

indicators.note: the synonym loses its starting letter, so it does not get started

parts.note: dreams are fantasies or imaginings

explanation.surface: Many daydreams that never come to anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally bundles of paper sheets, used informally to mean a large quantity.

clue.text: An idiot's place in Belgium

parts.note: a twerp is a silly or foolish person, an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool's home in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port city in Flanders, northern Belgium, famous for diamonds.

clue.text: Paint I'm mixing for instruments

indicators.note: mixing means blending together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist mixing paints to decorate musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums of an orchestra are percussion instruments.

clue.text: Wreck siege weapon that's retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word is read in the reverse direction, upwards in a down clue

parts.note: a ram, or battering ram, is a siege weapon for breaking gates

explanation.surface: A battering ram being wrecked as the besiegers fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or damage something is to ruin or wreck it.

clue.text: One playing a minor role exceptionally

definitions.meaning: a film walk-on or background actor with no lines
as an adverb, as in ... careful, it means unusually or especially

explanation.surface: An actor in a bit part who performs exceptionally well.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd-scene film actor is a walk-on; as an adverb the word also means especially.

clue.text: Pine for the holiday season?

parts.note: pine reads as longing for the holidays, but it is a conifer decorated in December

explanation.surface: Longing for the festive holidays to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb meaning yearn; it is the tree, a fir or pine brought indoors in December.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorated evergreen conifer put up in homes for the December festival.
